label: Aggregator
description: Accumulates iterator output using math operations or collection builders.
features: Collect values produced by Iterator or streaming dominos and emit the final result only once.
Supports sum, subtract, multiply, divide, min, max, array append and object map operations.
Initial seed can be defined statically or driven dynamically through the value_in_1 pin, while the main stream input uses value_in.
Stores progress in local state so concurrent iterators do not collide.

fields.heading: Input
fields.description: Value emitted each loop; aggregator reduces it using the selected Operation.

fields.heading: Operation
fields.description: Defines how each Input updates the accumulator.

fields.heading: Initial Value
fields.description: Seed applied before the first item. Defaults to 0 (arrays default to [] and objects to {}).

fields.heading: Key
fields.description: Optional key for object mode; can also be derived from iterator payload { key, value }.

pinStructure.exec_out: Fires once after the iterator reports done.
pinStructure.value_in: Accepts each numeric/object payload to aggregate.
pinStructure.key_in: Used for object aggregation when building key/value maps.
pinStructure.value_out: Exposes the final accumulator (populated on the last call only).

label: API Call
description: Send an HTTP request with axios and forward the JSON response to downstream nodes.
features: Supports GET, POST, PUT and DELETE using axios with automatic JSON parsing.
Url, method, headers and body can be configured statically or overridden through the value_in payload.
Runtime errors bubble up with useful status information so retries or error paths can react.
Response body is emitted on value_out for chaining into other dominos.

fields.heading: Url
fields.description: Endpoint to call. Connect value_in with a payload containing { Url } to override dynamically.

fields.heading: Method
fields.description: HTTP verb. Override by sending { Method: 'POST' } through the value payload.

fields.heading: Headers
fields.description: Key/value headers object merged into the axios request; can be overridden by ctx.input.Headers.

fields.heading: Body
fields.description: JSON payload for POST/PUT requests. Send { Body: {...} } through value_in to drive it dynamically.

pinStructure.exec_in: Runs the HTTP call when upstream execution arrives.
pinStructure.exec_out: Emits after the HTTP request finishes.
pinStructure.value_in: Accepts overrides object (Url, Method, Headers, Body).

label: API Trigger
description: Expose the workflow as an HTTP endpoint that can accept optional body/file uploads.
features: Generates a signed /workflow/{id}/trigger/{Function} URL for external callers.
Optional body/file requirements automatically expose a value_out pin containing the inbound payload.
Sanitises config-only fields so downstream nodes see only caller-supplied data.
Acts as a workflow entrypoint and does not expect exec_in.

fields.heading: Api Url
fields.description: Read-only URL that external systems should POST to.

fields.heading: Function
fields.description: Unique identifier appended to the trigger URL.

fields.heading: Require File Upload
fields.description: When enabled, value_out carries uploaded file metadata and validators enforce multipart input.

fields.heading: Require Body
fields.description: Expect JSON body; exposes the parsed payload on value_out.

pinStructure.exec_out: Fires when an HTTP call hits this trigger.
pinStructure.value_out: Populated only if Require Body/File Upload is enabled; contains cleaned input data.

label: Arithmetic
description: Evaluate a sequence of numeric inputs and operators ( + - * / % ^ ).
features: Support for unlimited operands by adding Input_n/Operator_n pairs.
Each operand/operator can be overridden at runtime via pins or by passing { Input_n } in the value payload.
Returns the computed scalar on value_out for downstream math or comparisons.
Performs strict numeric coercion and raises descriptive errors for invalid values.

fields.heading: Input_1
fields.description: First operand. Additional operands use headings Input_2, Input_3, ... with pins value_in_2, value_in_3, etc.

fields.heading: Operator_1
fields.description: Operator applied between Input_1 and Input_2. Use Operator_2 for Input_2/Input_3, etc.

fields.heading: Input_n
fields.description: Placeholder to indicate you can append as many Input_k + Operator_k pairs as needed.

pinStructure.exec_out: Continues after the computation.

label: Condition
description: Compare two values and branch execution on true/false results.
features: Supports equality, inequality, greater/less, contains/not_contains comparisons.
Value pins keep Text1/Text2 inputs synced when wires are attached.
True path leaves through exec_out, false path through exec_out_1.
Result boolean is emitted on value_out for additional logic.

fields.heading: Text1
fields.description: Left-hand operand.

fields.heading: Text2
fields.description: Right-hand operand.

pinStructure.exec_out: True branch.

label: Connector
description: Barrier that waits for multiple exec_in branches and merges their payloads before continuing.
features: Dynamically configurable number of exec_in handles (Case_0, Case_1, ...).
Stores partial payloads in local state until all branches arrive, then emits merged data.
Prevents downstream nodes from running until every prerequisite branch is complete.
Automatically clears state once exec_out fires.

fields.heading: Case_n
fields.description: Each case row corresponds to an exec_in handle (exec_in, exec_in_2, ...). Names are informational.

pinStructure.exec_in: Add as many exec_in_1, exec_in_2, ... handles as needed; connector waits for all of them.
pinStructure.exec_out: Fires exactly once after every branch has arrived with its payload merged.

label: CSV Writer
description: Convert arrays/objects into a CSV file and optionally upload it to GCS.
features: Accepts JSON arrays from the value_in pin or free-form text pasted into the Input Box.
Supports configurable delimiters, header handling and the ability to treat the first line as headers for text mode.
Uploads to Google Cloud Storage via the backend GCS service and returns asset metadata.
Falls back to local filesystem writes if GCS is unavailable.

fields.heading: Name
fields.description: Display name stored with the generated asset.

fields.heading: Input Box
fields.description: Used when Input Type = text.

pinStructure.exec_out: Continues after the file is written/uploaded while passing file metadata in the exec context.

label: Delay
description: Pause execution for a configurable number of milliseconds before continuing.
features: Accepts exact millisecond durations and blocks downstream exec until the timer completes.
Can be cancelled via abort signals when workflows are aborted.
Passes the inbound value through unchanged after the delay.
Useful for rate limiting, polling, or giving external systems time to settle.

fields.heading: Delay
fields.description: Milliseconds to wait before emitting exec_out.

pinStructure.exec_out: Fires after the delay.

label: Filter
description: Filter arrays, primitives or objects using field/value comparisons.
features: Supports primitive arrays and arrays of objects with per-field comparisons.
Operators include equals, contains, not_contains and numeric comparisons.
Single-object/primitive mode can short-circuit downstream execution when the predicate fails.
Property and Filter Value inputs can be wired for dynamic criteria.

pinStructure.exec_out: Runs with the filtered collection or halts when predicate fails in single-value mode.

label: Iterator
description: Loop over arrays or objects, emitting each item and an on-complete signal.
features: Accepts arrays/objects via value_in or generates numeric ranges when no input is provided.
Range Start/End restrict slices; Max flag forces iterating the entire collection regardless of range.
Order can be forward or reverse.
exec_out fires for each element while exec_out_1 fires once after completion.

pinStructure.exec_out: Per-item branch.
pinStructure.value_out: Current item (primitive or { key, value } for objects).

label: Mapper
description: Rename object keys (top-level) in objects or arrays of objects.
features: Input can be a single object or an array of objects.
Define rename pairs via Input_n fields that each hold [from, to].
PreserveOtherData flag controls whether untouched fields are retained or dropped.
Non-object inputs pass through unchanged.

fields.heading: Input_n
fields.description: Each entry stores a [from, to] tuple for renaming.

label: Print
description: Log or display a value for debugging. NOT for building strings to pass to other nodes.
features: IMPORTANT: Print is a debugging/logging tool only. Do NOT use it to build prompt strings or format data for downstream nodes.
To concatenate or format text for passing to another node (e.g. the AI domino), use the Join Text domino instead.
Supports {{placeholder}} token replacement with keys from ctx.input.
If no template is defined, prints the entire inbound object as JSON.
Resulting string is emitted on value_out but should only be used for terminal output or Response nodes, not for chaining into processing nodes like AI.

fields.heading: Text
fields.description: Template string that may contain {{variable}} tokens. For debugging/display only.

label: Read File
description: Load spreadsheets, PDFs, DOCX, JSON, and common text files from uploads, URLs, GCS, or raw base64 buffers (e.g. email attachments).
features: Accepts the ENTIRE email payload on value_in — it recursively scans the object and automatically finds and decodes the first attachment ({ name, mime, buffer }) without needing a Map or Code Runner node.
To process an email attachment: connect Email Trigger value_out directly to Read File value_in. No intermediate extraction step required.
Supports { key, url, bucket } for GCS files, a direct URL string, or an inline attachment { name, mime, buffer (base64) } anywhere nested in the input.
Parses: PDF → plain text, DOCX → plain text, XLSX/CSV → row arrays, JSON → parsed object, HTML/XML/TXT → text.
Auto-detects file type at runtime using filename, MIME type, and file signatures.
value_out emits the parsed content (string for text/PDF/DOCX, array for spreadsheets, object for JSON).

fields.heading: File
fields.description: Accepts the whole email payload object from Email Trigger value_out — automatically finds the first attachment. Also accepts { key, url, bucket }, a URL string, or a bare attachment object { name, mime, buffer (base64) }.

label: Google Drive
description: Upload a file or run bulk actions in Google Drive.
features: Attach a Drive connection identifier and upload files via the workflow UI.
Accepts runtime overrides for connection, file metadata, or destination path.
Emits uploaded file metadata for downstream processing.
Run bulk tag, move, rename, or access updates across multiple files.

fields.heading: Connect
fields.description: Drive connection name or vault id.

fields.heading: Action
fields.description: Choose upload or bulk action mode.

fields.heading: File Upload
fields.description: File object { key, url, name, size } or uploaded asset reference.

fields.heading: Full Path
fields.description: Destination path in Drive, e.g. /My Drive/Folder/file.ext.

fields.heading: Bulk Action
fields.description: Bulk action to apply: tag, move, rename, or access.

fields.heading: Targets
fields.description: One path per line or JSON array of { path, id }.

fields.heading: Tags
fields.description: Comma-separated tags to apply.

fields.heading: Destination Path
fields.description: Folder path to move files into.

fields.heading: Rename Template
fields.description: Rename template (supports {name} and {ext}).

fields.heading: Access Role
fields.description: Access role for permissions.

fields.heading: Access Type
fields.description: Access type: user, group, domain, or anyone.

fields.heading: Access Email
fields.description: Email address for user or group access.

fields.heading: Access Domain
fields.description: Domain for domain-wide access.

pinStructure.exec_in: Starts the Drive upload or path resolution.
pinStructure.exec_out: Continues after the Drive operation completes.
pinStructure.value_action: Selects upload or bulk action mode.
pinStructure.value_file: Supplies the file metadata or upload reference.
pinStructure.value_bulk_action: Selects the bulk operation to run.
pinStructure.value_bulk_targets: Provides target file paths or ids.
pinStructure.value_bulk_tags: Supplies tag values for bulk tagging.
pinStructure.value_bulk_destination: Supplies the destination folder for bulk moves.
pinStructure.value_bulk_rename_template: Supplies the rename template for bulk rename.
pinStructure.value_bulk_access_role: Supplies the permission role for bulk access.
pinStructure.value_bulk_access_type: Supplies the permission type for bulk access.
pinStructure.value_bulk_access_email: Supplies the email for bulk access.
pinStructure.value_bulk_access_domain: Supplies the domain for bulk access.
pinStructure.value_out: Outputs file metadata and Drive location info.

label: Google Drive Download
description: Download a file from Google Drive into the workflow.
features: Connects to a Drive vault and fetches a file by full path.
Stores the downloaded file in storage for downstream use.
Outputs file metadata and a storage URL.

fields.heading: Connect
fields.description: Drive connection name or vault id.

fields.heading: Full Path
fields.description: Drive path to download, e.g. /My Drive/Folder/file.ext.

pinStructure.exec_out: Continues after the Drive download completes.
pinStructure.value_full_path: Specifies the Drive path to download.
pinStructure.value_out: Outputs file metadata and storage location.

label: Slack Trigger
description: Start workflows from Slack channel messages using a connected Slack app.
features: Propagates Slack OAuth vaultId and slackChannelId to backend for event subscriptions.
Automatically unwraps Slack message payloads so downstream nodes receive user, text, ts, files, etc.
Bot invite helper ensures the Dominofy app is present in the selected channel.
value_out always contains the cleaned event payload.

fields.heading: vaultId
fields.description: Slack connection / vault identifier obtained from OAuth.

fields.heading: slackChannelId
fields.description: Channel to subscribe to.

label: Slack Action
description: Post messages to Slack channels or threads using a stored connection.
features: Accepts vaultId (connection), channelId and text from static config or runtime value pins.
Optional thread_ts lets you reply in an existing Slack thread.
Uses the shared SlackService backend so tokens are never exposed to the workflow JSON.
value_out exposes Slack response (channel + ts).

fields.heading: thread_ts
fields.description: Optional thread timestamp.

label: Email Trigger
description: Start workflows when a connected Gmail inbox receives a new email.
features: Matches Gmail notifications against the selected connection and optional inbox address filter.
Emits the full normalized email payload on value_out — see outputSchema for all available fields.
Requires a Gmail OAuth connection; Pub/Sub watch or polling drives triggers.
Use hasAttachments (boolean) from value_out to branch on whether the email has files.
Each attachment object contains name, mime, size, and base64-encoded buffer.

fields.heading: vaultId
fields.description: Gmail connection / vault obtained via OAuth.

fields.heading: inboxAddress
fields.description: Lower-case recipient address to match. Leave blank to trigger on any email for this Gmail connection.

outputSchema.description: The object emitted on value_out when an email arrives.

fields.emailAddress: The inbox address that received the email.
fields.subject: Email subject line.
fields.internalDate: Unix timestamp (ms) of when Gmail received the message.
fields.hasAttachments: Boolean — true if the email has one or more attachments.
fields.attachments: Array of attachment objects. Each contains: name (filename), mime (MIME type), size (bytes), buffer (base64-encoded file content), attachmentId, partId, contentId, contentDisposition.

label: Email Action
description: Send emails through a connected Gmail account with optional HTML and reply metadata.
features: Uses vaultId to pull Gmail tokens server-side; workflow JSON never stores secrets.
to, subject, body, html and from can be provided statically or via value pins for dynamic templates.
value_out returns the Gmail messageId for logging or threading.

fields.heading: from
fields.description: Optional from override; defaults to connection fromEmail.

label: Switch
description: Multi-branch switch that routes execution based on matching string cases.
features: Input value can be static or provided via value_in.
Add unlimited cases; the default branch uses exec_out and later cases continue as exec_out_1, exec_out_2, ... .
Unmatched inputs fall through to exec_out.
Case values can also be overridden through dedicated value_in, value_in_1, value_in_2, ... pins.

fields.heading: Case_n
fields.description: Each case row defines the string to match for exec_out_1, exec_out_2, and so on, while the default branch uses exec_out.

fields.heading: Case_Default
fields.description: Optional label for default branch.

pinStructure.exec_out: Used when no cases match.
pinStructure.exec_out_1: Emitted for matching case 1; additional cases continue as exec_out_2, exec_out_3, and so on.

label: AI
description: Send a prompt to an AI language model (Gemini/Vertex) and receive a text response.
features: Accepts a static prompt or a dynamic prompt supplied via value_in.
Supports Gemini API (via GOOGLE_API_KEY) or Vertex AI (via ADC) with automatic model fallback.
Returns generated text on value_out for chaining into print, response, or further processing nodes.
Prompt field supports plain text or templated instructions.

fields.heading: Prompt
fields.description: The instruction or question sent to the AI model. Connect value_in to supply a dynamic prompt.

pinStructure.exec_out: Continues after the model responds.
pinStructure.value_in: Accepts a dynamic prompt string to override the static field.
pinStructure.value_out: The generated text response from the model.

label: Response
description: ONLY use this domino when the workflow starts with an API Trigger (webhook). It sends the HTTP response back to the caller. Do NOT use it for email, scheduler, Slack, or any other trigger type — those workflows have no HTTP caller to respond to.
features: Exclusively for API Trigger workflows — it closes the HTTP request/response cycle.
Acts as a terminal node — no exec_out; workflow execution stops here.
Connect value_in to return dynamic data (e.g. AI output, database result) as the HTTP response body.
NEVER add this node to workflows triggered by Email, Scheduler, Slack, or other event-based triggers.

fields.heading: Response
fields.description: The value to return as the HTTP response body. Connect value_in to pass a dynamic value from upstream nodes.

pinStructure.exec_in: Triggers the HTTP response and ends execution.
pinStructure.value_in: Accepts the final value to be sent back as the HTTP response body.

label: Scheduler
description: Trigger the workflow automatically on a recurring schedule (minute, hour, day, week, month).
features: Supports once, minute, hour, day, week, and month frequencies.
Interval field sets how many minutes/hours between runs for sub-daily frequencies.
Weekly mode allows selecting specific days of the week.
Time zone aware — run times are evaluated in the configured zone.
Active toggle enables or disables the schedule without removing the node.

fields.heading: Active
fields.description: Enable or disable the schedule.

fields.heading: Frequency
fields.description: How often the workflow should run.

fields.heading: Interval
fields.description: Number of minutes or hours between runs (used for minute/hour frequencies).

fields.heading: Time
fields.description: Time of day to run (used for day/week/month frequencies).

fields.heading: Days of Week
fields.description: Days to run on (weekly frequency only).

fields.heading: Time Zone
fields.description: IANA time zone string, e.g. America/New_York. Defaults to browser local time.

pinStructure.exec_out: Fires at each scheduled interval, triggering downstream nodes.

label: Database Write (save/insert — use this to store data)
description: WRITE-ONLY: save, insert, update, upsert, or delete records. This is the ONLY domino that can persist data. Whenever the goal is to store or save something, use this — never storageRetrieve.
features: Use this when you need to SAVE or PERSIST data — e.g. store a score, log a result, record an event.
Supports create, update, upsert, and delete operations.
Document Key field uniquely identifies a document within a collection.
Data field (value_in_1) accepts a JSON object or string to store as the document body.
Returns the saved document and action metadata on value_out.

fields.heading: Collection
fields.description: Name of the collection to write to.

fields.heading: Operation
fields.description: The write operation to perform.

fields.heading: Document Key
fields.description: Unique key for the document. Required for update/upsert/delete.

fields.heading: Data
fields.description: JSON object to store as the document body.

pinStructure.exec_out: Continues after the document is saved.
pinStructure.value_in: Accepts a payload with Collection, Operation, Document Key, or Data overrides.
pinStructure.value_out: Returns { ok, action, collectionId, document } metadata.

label: Database Read (fetch only — cannot save)
description: READ-ONLY: fetch/query existing records. This domino CANNOT save, insert, or write data. For saving data use the storage (Database Write) domino instead.
features: Supports fetching a single document by key or all documents in a collection.
Limit field caps the number of returned documents.
Returns full document data including metadata on value_out.
Scoped to the current workflow's storage namespace.

fields.heading: Collection
fields.description: Name of the collection to read from.

fields.heading: Operation
fields.description: Fetch a single document by key or all documents in the collection.

fields.heading: Document Key
fields.description: Key of the document to retrieve (used for document operation).

fields.heading: Limit
fields.description: Maximum number of documents to return for collection queries.

pinStructure.exec_out: Continues after documents are fetched.
pinStructure.value_out: Returns { ok, action, collectionId, count, document, documents }.

label: Constructor
description: Build an object from multiple key/value pairs. Each row defines the output key and accepts a typed or connected value.
features: Create an object by adding as many Key_n / Value_n rows as needed.
Each Value_n can be entered directly or provided dynamically through its matching value_in_n pin.
Empty keys are ignored, and later duplicate keys overwrite earlier ones.
Outputs a single object on value_out for downstream nodes.

fields.heading: Key_1
fields.description: Key name for the first object property.

fields.heading: Value_1
fields.description: Value for the first property. Can be typed directly or connected from an upstream value pin.

fields.heading: Key_n
fields.description: Additional property names.

fields.heading: Value_n
fields.description: Additional property values; each can be typed or connected.

pinStructure.exec_out: Continues after the object is built.
pinStructure.value_in_1: First dynamic property value. Each Value_n gets its own value_in_n pin.

label: De-Construct
description: Extract one or more properties from an object or elements from an array. Use this — not Custom Code — whenever you need to pull fields out of a payload (e.g. extract 'hasAttachments' from an email, or 'messageId' from an email payload).
features: Set Type to 'object' to extract named keys from an object. Each Key_n holds the property name and outputs the value on value_out_n.
Set Type to 'array' to extract elements by index. Each Key_n holds the integer index and outputs the element on value_out_n.
Connect the source object/array to value_in (Input).
Each Key_n field has its own output pin value_out_n — connect downstream nodes to the specific output pin you need.
Always prefer De-Construct over Custom Code for simple property extraction.

fields.heading: Input
fields.description: The object or array to deconstruct. Connect the upstream value_out here.

fields.heading: Type
fields.description: Whether the input is an object (extract by key name) or an array (extract by index).

fields.heading: Key_1
fields.description: Property name (object mode) or index (array mode) for the first output. The extracted value is emitted on value_out_1.

fields.heading: Key_n
fields.description: Additional keys/indices. Each Key_n emits its value on value_out_n. Add as many as needed.

pinStructure.exec_out: Continues after extraction.
pinStructure.value_out_1: The value extracted by Key_1. Each Key_n has a corresponding value_out_n.

label: Join Text
description: Concatenate multiple text inputs into a single string. Use this — not Print — whenever you need to build a string to pass to another node (e.g. combining a static AI instruction with dynamic data).
features: The correct way to combine a static instruction with dynamic runtime data before sending to the AI domino.
Add as many Input_n fields as needed; they are joined in order with no separator.
Input_1 can be a static string (e.g. 'Score this resume from 1-100:'), Input_2 connected to a dynamic value_in_1 pin, and later inputs continue as value_in_2, value_in_3, and so on.
Result is emitted on value_out for passing to downstream nodes such as the AI domino's value_in.
Always prefer Join Text over Print when the goal is to build a string for further processing.

fields.heading: Input_1
fields.description: First text segment. Add Input_2, Input_3, … for additional segments.

fields.heading: Input_n
fields.description: Additional text segments joined in order after Input_1.

pinStructure.exec_out: Continues after the string is joined.
pinStructure.value_in_1: Dynamic pin for Input_2; additional segments continue as value_in_2, value_in_3, and so on.

label: SQL Runner
description: Execute a raw SQL query against an external PostgreSQL database connection.
features: Connect to any PostgreSQL database using host, port, database, user, and password.
Write SQL queries directly in the node or open the full-screen SQL editor.
Returns query results (rows) or row count metadata on value_out.
exec_out fires on a successful query; exec_out_1 fires on failure.
Connection credentials are managed locally and never stored in workflow JSON.

fields.heading: Query
fields.description: SQL statement to execute against the connected database.

fields.heading: Connection
fields.description: Opens the database connection configuration modal.

pinStructure.exec_in: Runs the SQL query when triggered.
pinStructure.exec_out: Fires when the query completes successfully.
pinStructure.exec_out_1: Fires when the query throws an error.
pinStructure.value_out: Contains the query result rows or rowCount.

label: Custom Code
description: Execute arbitrary JavaScript in a sandboxed VM (vm2) and return the function result.
features: Runs JavaScript in an isolated vm2 sandbox with a 5-second timeout.
Define a named function entry point via the FunctionName field.
Add Variable_n rows to inject named variables into the sandbox scope.
Variable values can be driven dynamically from upstream pins.
exec_out_1 fires on runtime exceptions; value_out returns the function result.

fields.heading: FunctionName
fields.description: Name of the JavaScript function defined in Code that will be called as the entry point.

fields.heading: Code
fields.description: JavaScript code block. Must define the function named in FunctionName.

fields.heading: Variable_n_name
fields.description: Name of a variable injected into the sandbox scope.

fields.heading: Variable_n_value
fields.description: Default value for the variable; override via a connected value pin.

pinStructure.exec_out: Fires on successful execution.
pinStructure.exec_out_1: Fires when the code throws a runtime error.
pinStructure.value_in_1: First dynamic variable value pin; later variable rows continue as value_in_2, value_in_3, and so on.
pinStructure.value_out: Return value of the entry-point function.

label: Shopify
description: Interact with a Shopify store — get, list, create, update, or delete products, orders, and customers.
features: Authenticates via a stored Shopify Access Token vault; credentials never appear in workflow JSON.
Supports Products, Orders, and Customers resources.
Operations: get, list, create, update, delete.
Optional JSON parameters object allows passing filters, fields, or body data.
value_out returns the Shopify API response.

fields.heading: Shop Domain
fields.description: Your Shopify store domain, e.g. my-store.myshopify.com.

fields.heading: Access Token (Vault Id)
fields.description: Vault ID referencing the stored Shopify Admin API access token.

fields.heading: Resource
fields.description: The Shopify resource to operate on.

fields.heading: Operation
fields.description: The CRUD operation to perform on the resource.

fields.heading: Parameters (JSON)
fields.description: Optional JSON object with additional parameters (e.g. filters, body data for create/update).

pinStructure.exec_out: Continues after the API call completes.
pinStructure.value_out: Returns the Shopify API response body.

label: Note
description: Add a free-text annotation or comment to the canvas — does not affect workflow execution.
features: Double-click to enter edit mode and type any annotation text.
Background colour is customisable via the colour picker in the header.
Has no execution pins and is never run — purely a canvas documentation tool.
Useful for labelling sections, explaining logic, or leaving instructions for collaborators.

fields.heading: Text
fields.description: Annotation text displayed on the canvas.

fields.heading: Color
fields.description: Background colour of the note.
